title_en: Liu Xuejuan v. LG Company, Suning Center — consumer rights dispute
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 8 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests and Article 27 of the Product Quality Law, if a cosmetics business operator marks a 'use-by qualified date' on the packaging of cosmetics with a limited use period but does not explain the exact meaning of that date, causing consumers to be unable to understand the safe use period of the cosmetics, such conduct infringes upon the consumers' right to know.
keywords_en: Civil; Consumer rights dispute; Second instance; Intermediate People's Court; Jiangsu Province; Zhejiang Province; Natural person; Legal person; Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests; Product Quality Law; Whether marking the use period after opening on cosmetics outer packaging is a statutory obligation; Whether the use-by qualified date covers the safe use period after opening; Dismissal of claims; Cosmetics purchase; Marking use-by date on outer packaging; Consumer requests to mark use period after opening; Trademark registration; Suning Center consumer rights dispute
full_text_en:
Liu Xuejuan v. LG Cosmetics Co., Ltd., Suning Universal Shopping Center — consumer rights dispute

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to Article 8 of the Law on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests and Article 27 of the Product Quality Law, where a cosmetics business operator has marked a "qualified expiration date" on the packaging of cosmetics with a limited period of use, but has not explained the precise meaning of such date, thereby causing consumers to be unable to understand the safe use period of the cosmetics, the business operator infringes upon the consumer's right to know.

Plaintiff: Liu Xuejuan, female, 25 years old, teacher at Nanjing TV University, Jiangsu Province, residing at Xuri Garden, Xuanwu District, Nanjing.

Defendant: Hangzhou LG Cosmetics Co., Ltd., Zhejiang Province, domiciled at: Hangzhou Economic and Technological Development Zone.
Legal Representative: Dai Zhenhua, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Defendant: Suning Universal Shopping Center, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, domiciled at: Hunan Road, Nanjing.
Legal Representative: Liu Xiaoyong, head of the center.

Plaintiff Liu Xuejuan filed a lawsuit with the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against Defendant Hangzhou LG Cosmetics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "LG Company") and Defendant Suning Universal Shopping Center (hereinafter "Suning Center") regarding a consumer rights dispute.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff purchased from Defendant Suning Center the "Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion" produced by Defendant LG Company. The outer packaging of this cosmetic product did not indicate the period of use after opening or the correct method of use. Having purchased such a cosmetic product, it is difficult for the plaintiff to use it correctly. LG Company's failure to correctly mark the outer packaging of the cosmetic product, and Suning Center's sale of such a product to consumers, infringes upon the plaintiff's right to know as a consumer. The plaintiff requests the court to order the defendants to: 1. Mark the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion and provide corresponding test reports; 2. Explain and mark the correct method of using the product or receiving the service.

The plaintiff submitted to the court the purchase invoice, the packaging box of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion, and four photographs to prove the facts alleged.

Defendant LG Company's Defense: The packaging box of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion contains instructions for use. The cosmetic product has been tested and has a test report before leaving the factory. Improper storage and use of cosmetics will affect their service life, so the shelf life after opening is difficult to determine. The plaintiff's request to mark the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of the cosmetics has no legal basis, and this claim should be dismissed.

Defendant LG Company submitted to the court the registration certificate for the Hai Xilan trademark, the enterprise standard filing number, the production license, the hygiene license, the inspection report from the Hangzhou Center for Disease Prevention and Control, and the packaging box and instructions for the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion, to prove that the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion it produces with approval is a qualified cosmetic product and that the correct method of use has been explained to consumers.

Defendant Suning Center's Defense: The plaintiff's claim exceeds the scope of industry practice and should not be granted.

Defendant Suning Center submitted to the court the joint sales counter contracts from December 2003 to December 2004, and the packaging box and instructions for the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion, to prove that it is a legitimate distributor of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion.

The court conducted examination and verification of the evidence. Upon examination, Defendants LG Company and Suning Center had no objection to the purchase invoice submitted by Plaintiff Liu Xuejuan, but argued that the hidden code on the product packaging box indicated that this particular box of Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion was not sold by Suning Center. Liu Xuejuan had no objection to the authenticity of the evidence submitted by LG Company and Suning Center.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, after trial, found that although Defendants LG Company and Suning Center denied that the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion held by Plaintiff Liu Xuejuan was purchased from Suning Center, they provided no evidence to prove this, so their denial was not upheld. Apart from this, both parties had no objection to the authenticity of the evidence submitted by the other party, which was confirmed. On this basis, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing conducted mediation. Liu Xuejuan considered that the instructions, test reports, and the in-court explanation of the correct method of use for the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion submitted by LG Company during the first instance satisfied her second claim, but she still requested LG Company and Suning Center to mark the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of the cosmetic product. LG Company and Suning Center argued that this claim of Liu Xuejuan had no legal basis and exceeded the scope of industry practice, so they could not agree. Both parties held their own views, and mediation was unsuccessful.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing held:

Article 5 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter "General Principles of Civil Law") stipulates: "The lawful civil rights and interests of citizens and legal persons shall be protected by law, and no organization or individual may infringe upon them." Consumers have the right to know the true circumstances of the products they purchase, use, or the services they receive, and have the right to request business operators to provide the validity period of the products based on the different circumstances of the products or services. The *Product Quality Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter "Product Quality Law") clearly stipulates that producers shall be responsible for the quality of the products they produce, and the markings on their products or packaging must be true. For products with a limited period of use, the safe use period shall be clearly marked in a conspicuous position. The Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion purchased by Plaintiff Liu Xuejuan has a clear mark on the bottom indicating that the expiration date is November 21, 2007, and there is no special explanation regarding this date. This date should be considered the safe use period that should be met both before and after opening. At present, neither national laws nor industry standards mandatorily require cosmetics to be marked with a period of use after opening. Therefore, Liu Xuejuan's request that Defendants LG Company and Suning Center mark the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of the cosmetics has no legal basis and is not supported.

Accordingly, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing rendered judgment on May 25, 2004:

The claims of Plaintiff Liu Xuejuan are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 50 and other litigation fees of RMB 100 shall be borne by Plaintiff Liu Xuejuan.

After the judgment was announced, Liu Xuejuan refused to accept it and appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province on the following grounds: 1. Article 27, paragraph 1, subparagraph (4) of the Product Quality Law stipulates: "For products with a limited period of use, the date of manufacture and the safe use period or the expiration date shall be clearly marked in a conspicuous position." The appellee first marked on the bottom of the outer packaging of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion "Expiration date recorded on bottom or side," and then marked the expiration period on the bottom of the container. This does not constitute marking the relevant period in a "conspicuous position" and violates this provision of the law. 2. It is well known that after opening, cosmetics come into contact with air, their active ingredients are prone to change, and the shelf life after opening will be greatly shortened. Consumers can only use cosmetics normally when they are in an opened state. The law requires producers to mark the safe use period or expiration date to protect consumers from harm by deteriorated cosmetics. "Qualified expiration date" only refers to the storage period of cosmetics in an unopened state, and does not include the "safe use period" or "expiration date" in the opened state that consumers need to know. Explaining "qualified expiration date" as "the safe use period that should be met both before and after opening" misleads consumers and infringes upon consumers' right to know. 3. The appellee claims that the shelf life of cosmetics after opening is difficult to determine; "difficult to determine" does not mean impossible to determine, but rather that the production enterprise has not done work in this regard. 4. Although the appellee's practice of marking the "expiration date" on the bottom of the product's outer packaging conforms to current national standards, current national standards cannot preclude higher requirements imposed on producers by law, nor can they prevent consumers from demanding the realization of rights granted by law. The appellant brought the lawsuit against the appellee precisely based on the provisions of the Product Quality Law. The first instance judgment dismissing the appellant's claims on the ground that they have no legal basis is clearly erroneous. The appellant requests that the first instance judgment be reversed and the appellant's claims be upheld.

Appellee LG Company argued in reply: Regarding the method of marking dates on general cosmetic labels, Section 64.1 of National Standard GB5296.3-1995 stipulates that "marking must be done in one of the following two ways: a. date of manufacture and shelf life; b. batch number and expiration date for use." "Qualified expiration date" refers to the normal period of use under normal storage conditions. Use within the period marked on the bottom of the bottle while meeting these two requirements can ensure quality. LG Company's marking of "qualified expiration date" on the outer packaging of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion complies with national and industry standards and is lawful. No cosmetics quality regulations, hygiene regulations, or national standards stipulate that cosmetics must be marked with a period of use after opening. The appellant's request to mark the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of cosmetics has no legal basis. The first instance judgment dismissing the appellant's claims is correct and should be upheld on appeal.

Appellee Suning Center argued in reply: "Qualified expiration date" means "the final date for quality assurance." The markings on the outer packaging of the cosmetic product in this case comply with national standards and are lawful. The second instance should uphold the first instance judgment.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, upon retrial, found:

On January 26, 2004, appellant Liu Xuejuan purchased from appellee Suning Center one bottle of Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion (for combination skin) produced by appellee LG Company, net content 130 ml, price RMB 170. The bottom of the outer packaging box of this cosmetic product was marked "Expiration date: recorded on bottom or side," and the bottom of the inner glass container was marked "Qualified expiration 2007.11.21." Liu Xuejuan opened and used the cosmetic product immediately after purchase. On March 8 of that year, Liu Xuejuan filed this lawsuit on the grounds that the outer packaging of the cosmetic product did not indicate the period of use after opening and the correct method of use, making it difficult for her to use the product correctly. Article 64 of Q330101, the *Enterprise Standard of Hangzhou LG Cosmetics Co., Ltd.*, provided by LG Company during the first instance trial, stipulates the storage conditions for the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion: "It shall be stored in a well-ventilated, dry warehouse with a temperature not exceeding 38°C. During stacking, it must be 20 cm from the ground, 50 cm from the inner wall, with passages left in the middle. It must not be placed upside down, and care must be taken to keep it away from water sources or heating. The first-in-first-out principle shall be strictly followed. Under stipulated storage conditions, with intact packaging and unopened, the shelf life of this product is four years."

During the second instance, appellant Liu Xuejuan stated that since appellee LG Company had provided the product instructions for use during the first instance, satisfying her second claim, she now only requests LG Company and Suning Center to mark the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of the cosmetic product and provide corresponding test reports.

Regarding the method of marking dates on the packaging of the cosmetic product involved in this case, the court consulted the General Administration of Quality Supervision, Inspection and Quarantine. The Administration replied: 1. The shelf life stipulated by national standards does not include the shelf life or expiration date for use of cosmetics in an opened state. 2. LG Company's enterprise standard stipulates a product shelf life of four years, and the expiration date for use refers to the period under appropriate storage conditions and in an unopened state. 3. The usable life of cosmetics after opening is greatly affected by environmental conditions and the user's personal habits. As the situations involved may vary widely, the shelf life after opening is difficult to determine uniformly.

The issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether the "qualified expiration date" marked on the packaging of the cosmetic product in this case includes the period of use after opening; 2. Whether marking the "qualified expiration date" on the cosmetic product in this case misleads consumers; 3. Whether LG Company's method of marking the cosmetic product in this case infringes upon consumers' right to know; 4. Whether the claim for marking the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion should be supported.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held:

Regarding issue one in dispute. Article 64 of Appellee LG Company's Q330101 *Enterprise Standard of Hangzhou LG Cosmetics Co., Ltd.* clearly stipulates: "Under stipulated storage conditions, with intact packaging and unopened, the shelf life of this product is four years." After opening, cosmetics come into contact with air. Coupled with changes in temperature and environment, as well as differences in the user's habits and hygiene conditions, their active ingredients are prone to change, and the shelf life after opening will be greatly shortened. The "qualified expiration date" of November 21, 2007, marked on the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion purchased by Appellant Liu Xuejuan on January 26, 2004, should refer to the shelf life of the product under stipulated storage conditions, with intact packaging, and in an unopened state, and does not include the period of use after opening. The first instance's finding that "this date should be considered the safe use period that should be met both before and after opening" is erroneous.

Regarding issue two in dispute. Consumers purchase cosmetics not for long-term storage, but for cleaning, protecting, and beautifying their skin. Once cosmetics deteriorate, they will harm the consumer's body through absorption and penetration by the skin. Therefore, what consumers are truly concerned about is not the shelf life of cosmetics in an unopened state, but the period of use after opening. To ensure the safety of life and property of consumers when using products, the Product Quality Law stipulates in Article 27, paragraph 1, subparagraph (4) that for products with a limited period of use, the date of manufacture and the safe use period or the expiration date shall be clearly marked in a conspicuous position. On the outer packaging of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion, Appellee LG Company only marked "qualified expiration date" without explaining that this date refers to the shelf life of the product in an unopened state. Furthermore, LG Company, during the first instance, interpreted "qualified expiration date" as: "under normal storage and normal use, do not exceed the date on the bottom of the bottle, to ensure quality." Even professionals in cosmetics production cannot correctly interpret the true meaning of "qualified expiration date." Consumers are not professionals, and without special explanation, it is reasonable for them to understand "qualified expiration date" as the safe use period after opening, which is their concern. Therefore, the practice of only marking "qualified expiration date" without simultaneously explaining the true meaning of such date does not enable consumers to correctly understand the safe use period of the cosmetic product and misleads consumers.

Regarding issue three in dispute. National Standard GB5296.3-1995 stipulates that on general cosmetic labels, the date of manufacture and shelf life, or the batch number and expiration date for use must be marked. The Product Quality Law stipulates that for products with a limited period of use, the date of manufacture and the safe use period or the expiration date shall be clearly marked in a conspicuous position. Looking at both provisions, the Product Quality Law merely imposes a higher requirement on the marking method for products with a limited period of use; there is no contradiction between the two. Article 8 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests* stipulates: "Consumers have the right to know the true circumstances of the products they purchase, use, or the services they receive." Producers of products with a limited period of use shall mark the safe use period of such products in a conspicuous position and clearly inform consumers. Appellee LG Company only marked "qualified expiration date" in accordance with national standards, but did not mark the safe use period of the product in accordance with the Product Quality Law, thereby infringing upon the right to know of Appellant Liu Xuejuan and other consumers.

Regarding issue four in dispute. Through the two instances of trial, Appellant Liu Xuejuan has understood that "qualified expiration date" refers only to the shelf life of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion in an unopened state. She now still requests Appellees LG Company and Suning Center to mark the period of use after opening on the outer packaging of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion. Regarding the period of use after opening for the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion, both LG Company and Suning Center stated that it is difficult to determine. According to law, as business operators of cosmetics, LG Company and Suning Center have an obligation to inform consumers of the safe use period of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion after opening in a clear and unambiguous manner, to ensure that consumers can safely use the cosmetic product. "Difficult to determine" does not mean impossible to determine. Enterprises should, with the aim of serving consumers, use methods such as directly marking the period of use after opening, explaining the true meaning of "qualified expiration date," or providing warnings about circumstances where the product should no longer be used, to help consumers fully understand and correctly use their products, and eliminate any misunderstandings consumers may have. LG Company and Suning Center's argument, based on the difficulty of determination, that Liu Xuejuan's claims should be dismissed is untenable.

Appellees LG Company and Suning Center have an obligation to inform consumers of the safe use period of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion after opening. In civil litigation, the law only protects the lawful rights and interests of specific civil subjects themselves. Therefore, the right holder and the subject matter in civil litigation must be specific. Although Appellant Liu Xuejuan's request that LG Company and Suning Center mark the period of use after opening on the packaging of the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion is reasonable, it involves non-specific right holders and subject matters, exceeding the scope that can be handled in this case, and is difficult to fully support. However, this claim includes Liu Xuejuan's desire to know the period of use after opening for the bottle of Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion she purchased. As a consumer, Liu Xuejuan enjoys the right to know, and this part of the claim is reasonable and lawful and should be supported.

In summary, the first instance incorrectly found the facts and erroneously dismissed all claims of Appellant Liu Xuejuan, which should be corrected by judgment according to law. Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, subparagraph (3) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, rendered judgment on March 10, 2005:

1. The first instance civil judgment is reversed.
2. Appellees LG Company and Suning Center shall, within three months from the date this judgment takes effect, inform Appellant Liu Xuejuan in writing of the period of use after opening for the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion she purchased.
3. The claim of Appellant Liu Xuejuan requesting that LG Company and Suning Center mark the period of use after opening on products identical to the Hai Xilan O² Time Firming Lotion she purchased is dismissed.

Court acceptance fees for the first and second instances total RMB 100, of which Appellant Liu Xuejuan shall bear RMB 20, and Appellees LG Company and Suning Center shall each bear RMB 40.

This judgment is final.
